speaker: Unknown
en: Hey folks, Jeff Berman here.
zh: 各位好,我是 Jeff Berman。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, we are revisiting one of our favorite conversations from the 2025 Masters of Scale Summit, Reid Hoffman in conversation with the iconic author, Brene Brown.
zh: 今天,我们重访 2025 年 Masters of Scale 峰会上我们最喜欢的一场对话之一:Reid Hoffman 与标志性作家 Brene Brown 的对谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's full of heart and smart.
zh: 它充满了真心和智慧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two things you're sure to get a lot of when you join us at this year's event as well.
zh: 当你参加今年的活动时,也一定能收获很多这两样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's coming up soon, October 20th to 22nd in San Francisco.
zh: 活动即将举行,10 月 20 日至 22 日,在旧金山。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to mastersofscale.com slash summit to learn more.
zh: 请访问 mastersofscale.com/summit 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi!
zh: 你好!

speaker: Unknown
en: Clearly, you have some fans here already.
zh: 显然,你在这里已经有一些粉丝了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like it.
zh: 我喜欢这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Howdy!
zh: 你好啊!

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a new book out called Strong Ground, which explores many aspects of what you call, and what should be called, courageous leadership.
zh: 你出了一本新书叫 Strong Ground,书中探讨了诸多你所说的、也是应该被这样称呼的「勇敢领导力」的方方面面。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, what is courageous leadership?
zh: 那么,什么是勇敢领导力?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I heard the word humility during the introduction.
zh: 嗯,我在刚才的介绍中听到了「谦逊」这个词。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to me, courageous leadership is a combination of a deep awareness of who you are and leading with discipline and accountability and humility.
zh: 对我来说,勇敢领导力是一种结合:对「你是谁」有深刻的认知,并以自律、担当和谦逊来领导。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about understanding that to lead is to serve others and not be served.
zh: 它关乎理解:领导意味着服务他人,而不是被服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's probably rooted in, above everything else, self-awareness.
zh: 而且我认为,它最根本的根基,大概在一切之上,是自我认知。

speaker: Unknown
en: About who you are and how you're showing up probably undergirds all of it.
zh: 关于你是谁、你如何展现自己,这大概是支撑这一切的基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what are some habits, principles, ways that you help people understand?
zh: 那么,有哪些习惯、原则或方法,可以帮助人们理解——

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they exhibiting it?
zh: 他们是否在展现勇敢领导力?

speaker: Unknown
en: What kinds of ways to build into it?
zh: 有哪些方式可以去构建它?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because obviously it's the right aspiration for everyone to get to courageous leadership, but it isn't just a slogan.
zh: 因为显然,达到勇敢领导力是每个人正确的追求,但它不只是一句口号。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually a way of being.
zh: 它其实是一种存在方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's interesting.
zh: 是的,这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the biggest finding possibly of my career has been that courage is teachable, measurable, and observable.
zh: 我认为我这辈子可能最大的发现就是：勇气是可教的、可测量的、可观察的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a skill set that's made up of four things.
zh: 它是一项由四件事组成的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: The ability to be very clear about your values and to assess whether you're behaving in a way that's aligned with them.
zh: 第一是能够非常清楚地了解自己的价值观，并评估自己的行为是否与之一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one thing to have values.
zh: 有价值观是一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's another thing to operationalize them and then hold yourself and your organization accountable for them.
zh: 把它们落地执行，然后让自己和整个组织为之负责，是另一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second is the ability to stay in your integrity and vulnerability.
zh: 第二是保持正直和展现脆弱的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vulnerability is very simply uncertainty, risk, and exposure.
zh: 脆弱很简单，就是不确定性、风险和暴露。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all of us are in it every day, all day.
zh: 所以我们每个人每天、全天都身处其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the ability to know when you're in it.
zh: 而能力就在于知道自己何时身处其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to not reach for armor.
zh: 并且不去抓取盔甲。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hypothesized early on that the biggest barrier to courageous leadership was fear.
zh: 我早期假设过，勇敢领导力的最大障碍是恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we went back to some of the leaders we were studying, they literally said some version of this to us.
zh: 当我们回去找一些我们正在研究的领导者时，他们确实对我们说过类似这样的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're going to make a list of brave leaders who are never afraid, don't put me on the list.
zh: 如果你要列一个从不害怕的勇敢领导者名单，别把我列进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm afraid every day.
zh: 我每天都在害怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, well, if it's not fear, what gets in the way of courage?
zh: 我当时就想，那如果不是恐惧，是什么阻碍了勇气？

speaker: Unknown
en: Armor.
zh: 盔甲。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's how we self-protect when we're afraid that's usually out of our awareness.
zh: 就是我们害怕时自我保护的方式，通常我们自己意识不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the things we do with leaders is what's your go-to armor?
zh: 所以我们对领导者做的事情之一就是：你的默认盔甲是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Mine is terrible.
zh: 我的很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mine is perfectionism, micromanagement.
zh: 我的是完美主义、微管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also get super decisive.
zh: 我还会变得超级果断。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's my armor.
zh: 那就是我的盔甲。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'll be in a meeting and yeah, I won't get paralyzed.
zh: 所以我会在会议里，是的，我不会陷入瘫痪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll be in a meeting and I'll be like, shut it down.
zh: 我会在会议里说，把它关掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, move the team, change the money.
zh: 不，把团队调走，把钱改了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not doing this.
zh: 我们不这么干了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I'll look up and I'll be like, oh shit.
zh: 然后我会抬头一想，哦糟了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know that these are good decisions.
zh: 我不知道这些是不是好决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And literally the last time I did that, my team looked back at me and said, we never write anything down when you're acting like this.
zh: 字面意义上，上一次我这么做的时候，我的团队看着我说，当你表现得这样时，我们从不写下任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, wait, what?
zh: 我说，等等，什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like, this is your armor.
zh: 他们说，这就是你的盔甲。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is my armor.
zh: 那确实是我的盔甲。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get overly decisive.
zh: 我会变得过度果断。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for us to be courageous, we have to know the very human ways that we self-protect when we're afraid.
zh: 所以要变得勇敢，我们必须了解自己在害怕时那些非常人性化的自我保护方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's some of the ways to kind of discover that armor and learn how to disarmor yourself?
zh: 有哪些方法可以发现那种盔甲，并学会卸下它？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think most of us know.
zh: 我认为我们大多数人都知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, if you want to ask someone, I wouldn't ask someone that works for you.
zh: 我是说，如果你要去问人，我不会问你手下的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because there's a power differential there that could make it super cringey for that person to describe exactly how you're an asshole.
zh: 因为那里存在权力落差，会让对方非常尴尬，没法精确描述你到底是怎么个混蛋法。

speaker: Unknown
en: What form of asshole-ness do I default to when I'm afraid?
zh: 我害怕时默认会表现出哪种形式的混蛋行为？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they'll be able to tell you for sure.
zh: 因为他们肯定能告诉你。

speaker: Unknown
en: They could tell you.
zh: 他们能告诉你的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they may smartly say, I don't know.
zh: 但他们可能会聪明地说，我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never seen it.
zh: 我从没见过。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's when you're too perfectionistic.
zh: 就是你太完美主义的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, yeah.
zh: 哦，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, no.
zh: 哦，不。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not the perfectionism.
zh: 别提完美主义了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your weakness?
zh: 你的缺点是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Perfectionism.
zh: 完美主义。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything I do is very good.
zh: 我做的一切都非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's not how it shows up for me.
zh: 但在我身上呈现出来的不是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Perfectionism is like maybe a month ago I gave the packing parachute speech.
zh: 完美主义就像是，大概一个月前，我发表了“打包降落伞”的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're packing parachutes.
zh: 我们在打包降落伞。

speaker: Unknown
en: 100% matters.

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want to jump out of a plane with a parachute that was packed at 90% excellence?
zh: 你想背着一个只以 90% 优秀程度打包的降落伞跳下飞机吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: People die.
zh: 人会死的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we were talking about a font choice.
zh: 而我记得我们当时在讨论的是一个字体的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: A parachute font coming soon to you.
zh: 降落伞字体即将与各位见面。

speaker: Unknown
en: A parachute font.
zh: 一种降落伞字体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't get this wrong.
zh: 别把这个搞错了。

speaker: Unknown
en: People will die.
zh: 人会死的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is all like a founder problem, but I have a therapist and a coach.
zh: 这完全是个创始人问题，但我有一位治疗师和一位教练。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm working on it.
zh: 我正在努力改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think you probably know, like, raise your hand if you could think about how you self-protect when you're in fear or uncertainty.
zh: 但我想你可能知道，如果你能想想自己在恐惧或不确定时是如何自我保护的，请举手。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you know.
zh: 我想你是知道的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't think you normally have to ask other people.
zh: 而且我认为你通常不需要去问别人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't have the insight or the courage to think about it, I question the sanity of you leading people.
zh: 如果你没有那样的洞察力或勇气去思考这个问题，我会质疑你领导别人的理智性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: To be honest with you, because who we are is how we lead.
zh: 跟你说实话，因为我们是什么样的人，决定了我们如何领导。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're not willing to have the humility to look into, can I get scary when I'm scared?
zh: 而如果你不愿意带着谦逊去审视——我害怕的时候会不会变得可怕？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of us can.
zh: 而且我想我们很多人都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can.
zh: 我会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, no, it's classic.
zh: 是啊，不，这很经典。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's classic.
zh: 很经典。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a legend.
zh: 我是个传奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you do intense research, you meet a lot of great CEOs, probably meet a lot of not great CEOs.
zh: 所以你做深入的研究，你见过很多很棒的 CEO，大概也见过很多不怎么样的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd say probably over the last decade or two,
zh: 我想说，大概在过去一二十年间，

speaker: Unknown
en: There was kind of more generally saying, hey, CO should be more empathetic.
zh: 有一种比较普遍的说法是，嘿，CEO 应该更有同理心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it seems to be going somewhat the other direction now.
zh: 而现在似乎在朝相反的方向走。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, sometimes people might describe that accurately as testosterone poisoning, which we have a certain amount of.
zh: 现在，有时人们可能会把它准确地描述为睾酮中毒，而我们身上确实有一定量这种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you seeing in this pattern of
zh: 在这个模式中你看到了什么——

speaker: Unknown
en: What kind of environments are CEOs operating in and what's the way to maintain kind of a true north for themselves, their organizations, their culture?
zh: CEO 们处于什么样的环境中，而他们要如何为自己、为组织、为文化保持某种真正的北极星？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the forces that are acting against it and what are the ways to navigate it?
zh: 有哪些力量在与它对抗，又有哪些方法可以应对？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I feel really lucky because I actually go to work every day.
zh: 是的，我感到非常幸运，因为我其实每天都会去上班。

speaker: Unknown
en: I spend probably 90% of my time working with C-suite and then level of direct reports under the C-suite.
zh: 我大概 90% 的时间都花在与高管层以及高管层直属下属级别的合作上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so optimistic in many ways because
zh: 我在很多方面都非常乐观，因为

speaker: Unknown
en: When you stop scrolling and you turn off the news and you're just sitting with people in a room, you see a lot of great people who wake up every day and are committed to doing the next right thing, regardless of what's in the zeitgeist right now.
zh: 当你停止刷手机、关掉新闻，只是和一群人坐在一个房间里，你会看到很多优秀的人，他们每天醒来都致力于去做下一件正确的事，不管当下时代潮流是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like that makes me very optimistic.
zh: 而我觉得这让我非常乐观。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in terms of the cultural push against empathy...
zh: 在文化上对同理心的抵制方面，我想说……

speaker: Unknown
en: I have two thoughts on that.
zh: 我有两点想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is just honest.
zh: 第一点就是诚实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, if my leadership plan includes hurting people, especially vulnerable populations, I'm gonna be against empathy.
zh: 你看，如果我的领导计划包括伤害别人，尤其是弱势群体，那我就会反对同理心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm gonna diminish and devalue empathy if part of my plan is to be hurtful because I don't need your pushback and your resistance.
zh: 如果我的计划里有一部分是要伤害人，我就会贬低和贬值共情，因为我不需要你的反驳和抵抗。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one.
zh: 这是一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing is empathy is very nuanced.
zh: 第二点是，共情是非常微妙的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's easy to grab the parts of empathy that are actually not very helpful.
zh: 所以人们很容易抓取共情中那些其实没什么帮助的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are two types of empathy.
zh: 共情有两种类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's cognitive empathy and effective empathy.
zh: 有认知共情和情感共情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you call me and you're like, hey, Bernay, I'm really having a hard time.
zh: 比如你打电话给我说，嘿，Bernay,我真的过得很艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I say, tell me what's going on.
zh: 我说，跟我说说发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you tell me what's going on.
zh: 然后你告诉我发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I reflect back and say, God, that sounds like incredibly disappointing.
zh: 我回应说，天哪，那听起来真是令人极度失望。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have a conversation and you feel seen and heard and believed.
zh: 我们进行了一次对话，你感到被看见、被听见、被相信。

speaker: Unknown
en: That empathy, that cognitive empathy is not only the source code for relationships, it's the source code of democracy, period.

en: What do you say when you're confronted with that?
zh: 当你面对这种情况时你会说什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the way to help them?
zh: 帮助他们的方法是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because obviously the game is moving very fast.
zh: 因为显然这场球赛变化非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is obviously on everyone's minds, how it integrates their lives, their organization's lives, their work's lives, et cetera.
zh: AI 显然在每个人的心头——它如何融入他们的生活、他们组织的生活、他们工作的生活，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's some of the work that you've been doing and lesson to say, hey, here are some principles to deal with this very chaotic, fast-moving game?
zh: 你一直在做哪些工作、有哪些经验教训可以说，比如，嘿，这里有一些应对这场非常混乱、快速变化的球赛的原则？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the first thing is I so respect a leader who has a self-awareness to say, I'm trying to pause and be strategic and thoughtful and I'm coming out of my skin.
zh: 我认为第一件事是，我非常尊重一个有自知之明的领导者，他能够说，我试着停下来，保持战略性和深思熟虑，而我其实已经焦虑得坐立不安了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first thing I would tell you is anyone that has the self-awareness to say that immediately gains my confidence.
zh: 我要告诉你的第一件事是，任何有自知之明能说出那番话的人，立刻就会赢得我的信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because so much of what's happening in terms of the world today is happening outside of the awareness of very senior leaders.
zh: 因为当今世界正在发生的很多事情，都发生在非常资深的领导者的觉察范围之外。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is a call that I had yesterday about relocating supply chain because of tariffs.
zh: 我是说，这是我昨天参加的一个电话会议，是关于因为关税而迁移供应链的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the leader just kept saying, we need to move fast.
zh: 那位领导者不断地说，我们需要快速行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we're looking for, and this is tricky.
zh: 我们所寻找的，这很微妙。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll be curious about what you think about this.
zh: 我会很好奇你怎么看这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to see urgency.
zh: 我想要看到紧迫感。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want productive urgency.
zh: 我想要有生产力的紧迫感。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to see risk-taking.
zh: 我想要看到冒险。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to see strategic risk-taking.
zh: 我想要看到战略性的冒险。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is the job of a leader today in this environment, given the political instability, technology, changing markets, I think the number one job outside of self-awareness of a leader today is to create time where none exists.
zh: 在当今这个环境中，鉴于政治不稳定、技术、变化的市场，领导者今天的工作——除了自知之明之外——首要工作就是创造本不存在的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Create time where none exists.
zh: 创造本不存在的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to understand that better, I had to turn to sport.
zh: 为了更好地理解这一点，我不得不转向体育。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so many sports metaphors.
zh: 体育隐喻实在太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Literally, the question I got from the Wall Street Journal is, did you feel comfortable putting a chapter around John Keats next to a chapter called The Tush Push?
zh: 字面上说，我从《华尔街日报》收到的问题是，你是否觉得把一篇关于约翰·济慈的章节放在一个叫「Tush Push」的章节旁边是合适的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, yeah, dude, why?
zh: 我就说，是啊，老兄，为什么这么问？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I'm like, do you like poetry?
zh: 我就像，你喜欢诗歌吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, yeah.
zh: 他说，喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, do you like football?
zh: 我就说，你喜欢橄榄球吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, yeah.
zh: 他说，喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like...
zh: 我就像……

speaker: Unknown
en: Shut it.
zh: 闭嘴吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, yeah, we can do both.
zh: 我就说，是啊，我们可以两者都要。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you turn to sports and you look at really talented athletes, it looks like they're slowing down the ball in play, but they're actually not creating more time between a serve and a return or a kick.
zh: 但如果你转向体育，看那些真正有天赋的运动员，看起来像是他们在比赛中让球慢了下来，但他们其实并没有在发球与回击或踢球之间创造更多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: What they're doing, and I think this is the future of leadership, is a very complex skill set of anticipatory awareness,
zh: 他们所做的——我认为这就是领导力的未来——是一个非常复杂的技能组合：预判性意识、

speaker: Unknown
en: Temporal awareness and situational awareness.
zh: 时间性意识和情境意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the leaders today are understanding how to read what they can't see.
zh: 所以今天的领导者正在学习如何读懂他们看不见的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: In football, we'd call it pocket presence.
zh: 在橄榄球里，我们称之为「口袋感知」。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a quarterback gets a snap, breaks back.
zh: 就像一个四分卫接到开球，后撤。

speaker: Unknown
en: He has three seconds to figure out how to move the ball down.
zh: 他有三秒钟的时间来弄清楚如何把球推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's a very complex group of skills that he has with his team around being able to see, to be able to read a field you can't see.
zh: 但这是他与周围团队一起拥有的一组非常复杂的技能，能够看见、能够读懂你看不见的球场。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the question I have for a lot of senior leaders is, where are you on anticipatory awareness?
zh: 所以我问很多资深领导者的问题是，你在预判性意识上处于什么位置？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are you in systems thinking?
zh: 你在系统思维上处于什么位置？

speaker: Unknown
en: These are the deep thinking skills moving forward.
zh: 这些是向前走的深度思考技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I completely agree.
zh: 是的，我完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of it is to realize that while it's moving very fast and you cannot create more time, your fitness function is not response at speed.
zh: 其中一部分是要意识到，虽然事情变化非常快，而你无法创造更多时间，但你的适应度函数并不是以速度做出响应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your fitness function is intelligent response at speed, right?
zh: 你的适应度函数是以速度做出智能响应，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the difference between urgency and productive urgency, between risk-taking and strategic risk-taking.
zh: 这就是紧迫感与有生产力的紧迫感之间的区别，冒险与战略性冒险之间的区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every CEO is saying, I need more risk-taking.
zh: 每一个 CEO 都在说，我需要更多冒险。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like, I was interviewing someone the other day and she said, no, I'm a get shit done, I'm a GSD kind of person.
zh: 这就像是，我前几天在面试一个人，她说，不，我是一个把事情搞定的人，我是一个 GSD（把事情搞定）类型的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, that I don't need.
zh: 然后我就说,那个我不需要。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I actually need is a GSSD, get strategic shit done.
zh: 我真正需要的是一个 GSSD,把战略性的破事干完。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because what you're seeing right now, and I'm curious if you're seeing this, you're seeing action over impact.
zh: 因为你现在看到的,我很好奇你是否也看到了,是行动多于影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Depends on the leader.
zh: 取决于领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does definitely happen.
zh: 这种情况确实会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously we've introduced like five to seven questions that we can go on for the next 30 minutes.
zh: 显然我们已经引入了大概五到七个问题,可以接着聊 30 分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh yeah.
zh: 哦是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the clock just ran out.
zh: 但时间刚刚到点了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes me 25 minutes to order a sandwich.
zh: 我点个三明治都要花 25 分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we did pretty, we did pretty good.
zh: 所以我们做得还,我们做得挺不错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as you can see, amazing.
zh: 大家可以看到,非常精彩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks, Franny.
zh: 谢谢,Franny。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank y'all so much.
zh: 非常感谢大家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks again to Brene Brown for joining us at the Masters of Scale Summit.
zh: 再次感谢 Brene Brown 来到 Masters of Scale 峰会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Her new book is Strong Ground, and we'll put a link in the show notes.
zh: 她的新书是 Strong Ground,我们会在节目备注中放一个链接。

speaker: Unknown
en: And while I have you, just a deep, deep thanks to everyone who came to Summit, not just those who appeared on stage, but who were in community, in conversation, looking for ways to build a better future.
zh: 趁大家还在,我要向所有来到峰会的人致以深深、深深的感谢,不仅是那些登上舞台的人,还有那些在社区中、在对话中、寻找建设更美好未来之途的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're so grateful to all of you, and we're excited to see you back in San Francisco next year.
zh: 我们非常感谢你们所有人,我们期待明年再见,在旧金山。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every business hits the same wall the moment your business outgrows the systems that got you here.
zh: 每一家企业都会撞上同一堵墙,当你的业务超出了让你走到今天的那套系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Spreadsheets everywhere, five different logins, data scattered across entities that don't even talk to each other.
zh: 表格到处都是,五套不同的登录账号,数据散落在彼此根本不通的各个实体之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your finance team spends more time finding data than using it, that's when you need the Intuit ERP.
zh: 如果你的财务团队花在找数据上的时间比用数据还多,那就是你需要 Intuit ERP 的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Intuit Enterprise Suite is the AI-native ERP solution that's powerful, painless, and proven, built for businesses scaling fast without the complexity that usually comes with it.
zh: Intuit Enterprise Suite 是 AI 原生的 ERP 解决方案,强大、无痛、经过验证,为快速增长的企业而打造,却没有通常伴随而来的复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: From the makers of QuickBooks, learn more at intuit.com slash ERP.
zh: 出自 QuickBooks 的缔造者,前往 intuit.com/ERP 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans will never be more intelligent than AI.
zh: 人类的智能永远不会超过 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's going to be two types of companies.
zh: 未来将有两类公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are great at AI and those that went out of business because they weren't.
zh: 一类擅长 AI,另一类因为不擅长而倒闭了。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we build a future that is human-centered?
zh: 我们如何构建一个以人为本的未来?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Rana Elkayubi, and on my podcast, Pioneers of AI, we answer that question and so many more.
zh: 我是 Rana Elkayubi,在我的播客 Pioneers of AI 上,我们回答这个问题以及更多更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an AI scientist, entrepreneur, and investor, I know what it takes to build AI that works for everyone.
zh: 作为一名 AI 科学家、创业者和投资人,我知道打造对每个人都管用的 AI 需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every week I sit down with the pioneers shaping our future, and we take you behind the scenes of the AI that's transforming our lives.
zh: 每周我都会与塑造我们未来的先驱者们坐下来,带你们走进正在改变我们生活的 AI 的幕后。

speaker: Unknown
en: Find Pioneers of AI wherever you tune in.
zh: 在你收听的任何平台搜索 Pioneers of AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey listeners, Bob here.
zh: 嘿,听众们,我是 Bob。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you listen to Rapid Response on Masters of Scale, you may be missing half the show because every Friday we release a second Rapid Response exclusively in the Rapid Response feed.
zh: 如果你收听 Masters of Scale 旗下的 Rapid Response,你可能错过了节目的一半,因为每周五我们会在 Rapid Response 频道独家发布第二期 Rapid Response。

speaker: Unknown
en: The guests and topics are just as compelling and timely from Ford's CEO to NASA's administrator to the lessons from the Devil Wears Prada.
zh: 嘉宾和话题同样精彩且切合时事,从 Ford 的 CEO 到 NASA 的局长,再到《穿普拉达的女王》带来的启示。

speaker: Unknown
en: It takes about...
zh: 只需要大约……

speaker: Unknown
en: 10 seconds to find.
zh: 10 秒钟就能找到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just search Rapid Response wherever you listen to podcasts and hit follow to make sure you never miss an episode.
zh: 只要在你收听播客的地方搜索 Rapid Response,点击关注,确保你不错过任何一集。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope to see you there.
zh: 我希望在那里见到你。

zh: Masters of Scale 是 Wait What 的原创节目。

zh: 我们的执行制片人是 Eve Trow。

en: Our senior producer is Trisha Bobita.
zh: 我们的高级制片人是 Trisha Bobita。

speaker: Unknown
en: The production team includes Masha Makotunina.
zh: 制作团队包括 Masha Makotunina。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our senior talent executive is Stephanie Stern.
zh: 我们的高级艺人总监是 Stephanie Stern。

zh: 混音与母带制作由 Aaron Bassinelli 和 Brian Pugh 完成。

zh: 原创音乐由 Ryan Holiday 创作。

zh: 我们的播客主管是 Leetal Mollad。

zh: 访问 mastersofscale.com 查找本集的文字稿并订阅我们的通讯。
